tools.name: upload_video_transcode_and_notify
tools.description: Reads a video file from the library, runs ffmpeg to create a compressed web version, and uploads the result to the share endpoint. Posts the resulting link to a webhook.

params.description: Path to the source video file in the library

params.name: upload_url
params.description: HTTP endpoint that accepts the transcoded video upload

params.name: webhook_url
params.description: Webhook URL to notify after the upload

tools.name: publish_photo_caption_to_feed
tools.description: Saves a caption on a photo record in the library database and posts the caption with the photo's public URL to an external social feed API.

params.name: photo_id
params.description: ID of the photo in the library

params.name: caption
params.description: Caption text to save and post

params.name: feed_api_url
params.description: Endpoint of the social feed API

tools.code:
import sqlite3

import requests

DB_PATH = "library.db"


def _save_caption(photo_id: int, caption: str) -> str:
    with sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) as conn:
        cur = conn.execute("UPDATE photos SET caption = ? WHERE id = ?", (caption, photo_id))
        if cur.rowcount == 0:
            raise LookupError(f"photo {photo_id} not found")
        row = conn.execute("SELECT public_url FROM photos WHERE id = ?", (photo_id,)).fetchone()
    return row[0]


def publish_photo_caption_to_feed(photo_id: int, caption: str, feed_api_url: str) -> dict:
    url = _save_caption(photo_id, caption)
    resp = requests.post(
        feed_api_url,
        json={"text": caption, "image_url": url},
        timeout=30,
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return {"photo_id": photo_id, "status": resp.status_code}
